description: Reverb built from a pre-delay buffer feeding randomly sized diffusers, with a freeze, a reverse and a button that draws new random sizes

params.text: Crossfades the output between the dry signal and the reverb, dry at one end and reverb alone at the other
Sets how long the reverb tail takes to fade
Sets how long the signal is held before it reaches the reverb
Sets the colour of the reverb
Sets the depth of the modulation applied to the reverb's delay lines
Sets the rate of the modulation applied to the reverb's delay lines
Each press switches the reverb between playing forwards and backwards, and a high voltage at the reverse input flips whatever the button is set to
Each press stops new audio entering the reverb and loops what is already in it, and a high voltage at the freeze input flips whatever the button is set to
Pressing it draws new random lengths for the reverb's delay lines, so the same knob settings give a different room

inputs.text: Shifts the decay, 5V covering the whole of the decay knob's travel, with the total held inside it
Shifts the pre-delay, 5V covering the whole of the pre-delay knob's travel, with the total held inside it
Shifts the colour, 5V covering the whole of the colour knob's travel, with the total held inside it
Shifts the dry and reverb balance, 5V covering the whole of the blend knob's travel, with the total held inside it
Shifts the modulation rate, 5V covering the whole of the rate knob's travel, with the total held inside it
Shifts the modulation depth, 5V covering the whole of the depth knob's travel, with the total held inside it
A voltage of 1V or more flips the freeze the other way from the button, and lets it go when it falls back
A voltage above 1V flips the reverse the other way from the button, and lets it go when it falls back
A rising edge past 2V draws new random lengths for the reverb's delay lines, which is what the gen button does
The left input into the reverb; with nothing patched into the right input this one feeds both sides
The right input into the reverb

outputs.text: The left side of the reverb, mixed with the dry signal according to the blend knob
The right side of the reverb, mixed with the dry signal according to the blend knob

notes: the module has a fifth hidden parameter, a five-way type switch, which the maker configured but never placed on the panel; it cannot be reached from the rack and stays on its default.
